Welcome to John Chilton School
I am honoured to be the Headteacher at John Chilton School with its experienced, skilled and dedicated staff and our fantastic pupils who are an inspiration to us all. Every day I take pride in the diverse community where we learn from each other, celebrate together and work as a team with our families.
Pupils said that they love coming to school.
“This is because staff are kind and take care of their needs. Pupils behave extremely well.Those that find meeting the school’s behaviour expectations challenging receive targeted and effective support. Pupils enjoy making new friends and look out for each other. There is a very happy and purposeful ambience that permeates across the school.Ofsted 2024”
The school strives to attend to the range of pupils’ individual needs
“Pupils leave the school very well prepared for the next stages of their education and adult living. Older pupils told inspectors that they feel ready for the ‘big world’. This is because the schoolprioritises a holistic and bespoke approach to meeting each pupil’s needs. Teaching, pastoral and therapeutic teams work in complete sync with each other. As a result, pupils make great gains in their academic, social, emotional, behavioural and physical development.Ofsted 2024”
The school provides pupils with an extensive range of enrichment activities.
“Many are aimed at nurturing their confidence and preparing them for independent living. For example, pupils run a café. They budget, purchase ingredients, bake cakes and sell a range of snacks. Their customers include pupils in the adjacent mainstream school. Pupils also run a delivery service for peers and staff who order online. Pupils are rightly proud of this work.Ofsted 2024”
The school has very high expectations for behaviour.
“Staff have frequent training in understanding the underlying causes of behaviour and how to respond to it. They consistently encourage and promote positive behaviours. The pastoral team deploys a range of bespoke strategies to support pupils to follow the school’s routines and expectations. These strategies are transformative. Ofsted 2024”

Ethos
John Chilton School is a welcoming and inclusive community where every pupil is supported to thrive academically, physically, socially and emotionally. Our skilled and dedicated staff provide an ambitious curriculum that responds to a broad range of physical and learning needs, encouraging curiosity, creativity and meaningful progress.
We promote emotional wellbeing, positive communication and self-regulation, fostering a strong sense of belonging and pride. Our environment and facilities are carefully designed to develop independence, build resilience, and prepare pupils for the challenges and opportunities of adult life.
Our staff team reflects the rich cultural diversity of our school and local community and is central to our commitment to being a proactive anti-racist school — one that empowers all pupils, staff and families to achieve, grow and feel valued. Through real-world learning, enriching experiences and a focus on personal growth, we support every young person to flourish as an active, fulfilled and contributing member of society.
Vision and Values
At John Chilton School, we strive for the development of confident, motivated and independent learners in a sociable, safe and accessible environment; supported by communication and engagement between home, school and partnerships.

pageCache.text:
Headteacher Welcome Message
The school is an exciting, stimulating and innovative place to learn and we take huge satisfaction in knowing our young people well, in striving for improvement and in providing them with an environment in which they feel safe, well-supported and encouraged to succeed. We ensure that we meet the differing needs of our pupils by adapting the environment, developing learning pathways and having specialist teams and resources throughout the school.
Our pupils deserve the very best educational opportunities, and we endeavour to help them achieve their best in terms of their learning, independence, confidence and motivation which are central to our ethos. We do this in partnership with the many professionals and other organisations with whom we work and chiefly, we aim to work in partnership with parents who know their children best. We are approachable and supportive; parents are always welcome to contact us to arrange a meeting to discuss their child’s provision and progress.
If you would like to visit John Chilton School, please contact the school office to arrange an appointment or arrange to speak with me if you have any queries.
Your children are unique. We feel honoured to assist their holistic development during their school years and can assure you that we will do whatever we can to make their time here happy and successful.
Sue RademacherHeadteacher

Ofsted February 2024
Pupils are taught about different faiths and visit places of worship… Pupils’ cultural development is well promoted..…Pupils enjoy visits from music and ballet companies. As part of a range of activities inspired by learning about the Windrush generation, pupils entered and won a local art competition linked to this theme. In addition, all pupils take part in a range of extra-curricular clubs every week.
Our bespoke curriculum motivates pupils to imagine, enquire and develop a sense of fascination about themselves, others and the world around them. We create opportunities for reflection on learning, ideas, opinions and behaviour. Pupils are supported to debate and discuss various topics, including moral issues surrounding internet use, social media and mobile phones.
We prioritise emotional development and relationship building, helping pupils develop self-knowledge and forge appropriate connections with others. Through our statutory PSHE, RSHE, and Tutor Time Curriculum, we reinforce these vital life skills.
Our school celebrates diversity through various enrichment activities, including:
Visits from artists, musicians, and performers from ballet, opera and theatre Cultural celebrations such as Diwali, Christmas and Eid School-wide events including Windrush Event, International Days and LGBTQ+ Awareness Week Talent showcases through JC’s Got Talent, Art Galleries and Musical performances
We actively participate in awareness campaigns like Mental Health Awareness Week, Show Racism the Red Card and Anti-Bullying Week. Our commitment to social responsibility extends to supporting various charities, including Children in Need, Jeans for Genes Dayand local Food Banks.
Our School Cluster Peer Review further reinforced this recognition, noting:
“Conversations with staff demonstrate how the strong values manifested by the leadership allow for all members of the school community to be visible and valued.”
The review particularly praised our café program, noting how it develops “social skills, communication skills, life skills, work skills- it is an authentic experience in which they are learning, linking to ambition to experience the world further.”
For current updates on our SMSC activities, please visit our News section Loading...

The school provides pupils with an extensive range of enrichment activities. Many are aimed at nurturing their confidence and preparing them for independent living. Pupils are rightly proud of this work
The school has very high expectations for behaviour. Staff have frequent training in understanding the underlying causes of behaviour and how to respond to it. They consistently encourage and promote positive behaviours. The pastoral team deploys a range of bespoke strategies to support pupils to follow the school’s routines and expectations. These strategies are transformative. Pupils’ behaviour in lessons is excellent. They pay attention, listen to each other and try hard. These positive attitudes play a major role in securing pupils’ high achievements.
The school offers pupils many excellent opportunities that aim to make a contribution to their personal development… They are helped to understand topics like personal space and are taken on multiple visits into the community, go shopping and practise using public transport. These experiences help them prepare for independent living.
Personal Development , Behaviour and Attitudes
The Personal Development of pupils is at the core of John Chilton School and embedded into the vision, environment, curriculum and events. We pride ourselves on our provision that is pupil-centred , understands the individual needs of the pupils to support behaviour for learning , self esteem, relationships and sense of identity. Each pupil’s individual and unique contribution is important and valued. We celebrate achievement, diversity and community engagement. We know that all pupils’ behaviours, skills, challenges and needs are diverse. We work as a strong, cohesive team to support pupils through therapies, interventions, play, lessons and transitions; understanding that all behaviour is a form of communication. An experienced team of staff all collaborate to best meet each pupil’s needs. Nurturing approaches are at the heart of what we do, ensuring staff understand our pupils’ learning styles and their differing needs. We are strategic and flexible to offer the best support, including consideration of attachment styles, trauma, adverse childhood experiences.
We work with key partners and therapists when providing input for Personal Development, Behaviour and Attitudes : Tender, Diversity Role Models, Workshops, Connexions, and the school’s Multi-Disciplinary Team that includes onsite therapeutic approaches , counselling specialists and our therapy dog. We have a specialist team of skilled staff to support behaviours, social and emotional needs, therapies, communication who all collaborate closely together. For many pupils we create individual behaviour plans and record and monitor behaviour data to implement and adapt impactful interventions.
Our Personal Development also includes carefully planned opportunities and links within PSHE, Relationships and Health education, careers support, links to community, class café, work experience, travel training and British Values
Building Respectful Relationships: Our Tender Partnership
We’ve partnered up with Tender Education and Arts (www.tender.org.uk) for whole school input to promote a culture of healthy, equal and respectful relationships for the benefit of our school culture and the futures of our learners. This links to our PSHE and RSHE curriculum but is embedded through our whole school ethos and values .
Through our workshops with Tender, our students cover topics like friendships, expressing emotions, consent, safety and boundaries in relationships. These are explored in age appropriate ways and delivered with sensitivity and awareness of respect and diversity.
Tender will continue to deliver in-school training, workshops and creative campaigns for staff and school community as part of our work.
John Chilton School is proud to be one of the first schools to achieve Healthy relationships Champion School Status

Most pupils are taught to read. The phonics programme is taught effectively by well-trained staff. Information from ongoing assessments informs bespoke group work and additional support. Pupils will also be able to access learning materials and ebooks on the Oxford Owl website – click here and here
In the primary department we will continue to use the Oxford Reading Tree scheme to ensure that pupils are exposed to a wider range of reading materials.
In the secondary department of John Chilton School, Bedrock Learning, an online vocabulary programme has been implemented to support pupils’ acquisition and learning of words. Pupils in the Purple and Red Phase 3 and 4 classes have been accessing this tool regularly since the spring term. Each pupil has an online account that is set to their appropriate level.
Pupils are given challenge words introduced through a passage of text. There are following questions and activities to help pupils embed their understanding of these words. Activities include finding synonyms and antonyms of words, word associations, or using the word in a sentence.
Pupils are able to complete tasks both in and out of school, as long as they have internet access. In fact, pupils are encouraged to access Bedrock Learning for home learning. Many of the activities are narrated, so headphones are recommended.
A tracker of vocabulary words that pupils are learning and have learned are generated to record pupils’ understanding. Teachers are able to monitor pupils’ progress through weekly reviews that Bedrock Learning conducts – click here.

Governing Body Information
The John Chilton School Governing Board is made up of a group of concerned members who have volunteered to help guide the school in its activities, supporting the staff and Headteacher.
They are involved in decisions about many aspects of leading and managing the school – such as running buildings and budgets, supporting staff and setting standards.
They help to make big decisions about the school’s long-term goals; ensuring that it is moving forward ambitiously.
They act as a ‘critical friend’ in a strategic role, and include Parents, Staff, Community members and representatives from the Local Authority.
If you have an interest in joining our Governing Board and wish to get involved in building a great future for our children and young people; having the time and commitment to join an energetic team, we would like to hear from you.
Please contact the Chair of Governors, via the school office and register your interest.
The Clerk to the Governing Board is Lorna Valcin.

Katie Yirrell
I have spent many years in the world of education; as a qualified teacher; a volunteer in my children’s schools; as a student 5 years ago at the Institute of Education to achieve a Masters in Special and Inclusive Education, and most recently and currently as a SENCo at an independent primary school in west London. I have also worked in retail for several years and ran a small business. I hope to bring these experiences with me as a committed Governor at John Chilton School, as well as my special interest in employment prospects for pupils with SEND.
Steve Garry
I joined the Governing Body of the school in February 2017. Previously I worked as a senior Finance Executive in the Telecommunications industry for 20 years and then for 10 years as a Maths Teacher in a state comprehensive school. This previous experience gives me a unique set of financial and educational skills which I hope to use to good effect for The John Chilton School. Now that I am a stay at home dad with two teenage children I serve as a Governor at two schools and I am also a Trustee of a Legal Aid Charity.
Daniel McNamara
I have over 13 years’ experience as a class teacher and middle leader across mainstream primary schools, special schools and specialist colleges, and have been part of JCS for nine years. Alongside this, I have supported children and young people with SEND through respite care charities and, more recently as a SEND curriculum adviser for a local café – helping young people with SEND move into employment.
Lydia Howarth
Lydia is a Mum of three. One of her children attended John Chilton for 16 years. She started out as a Social Worker supporting adults with Learning Disabilities. She is particularly interested in ensuring that the voices of children and young adults with disabilities are heard. She is also interested in supporting young people through the transition to adult services. She now has her own healthcare practice.
Sue Rademacher
As Headteacher at John Chilton School, I have a key relationship with fellow Governors. It is my responsibility to keep them well informed about the running of the school. At the same time Governor colleagues hold me to account for my leadership and its impact on the educational performance of the school, its pupils, as well as the management of the staff team.
I aim to work closely with the Governing Body to ensure a clarity of vision, ethos and strategic direction for John Chilton School for the benefit of the pupils and the whole school community.
Nadia Amani
With 15 years of experience in Accounting and Finance, I proudly serve as a Local Authority Governor at John Chilton School. My expertise lies in managing financial systems, forecasting fiscal trajectories, and promoting accountability across various sectors. Applying this knowledge to the education sector allows me to make a meaningful difference in children’s lives.
Combining financial acumen with a strong commitment to the community, I bring a unique perspective to contribute effectively to John Chilton School. As a dedicated member of the Ealing community, I am passionate about ensuring every child receives an exemplary education, which drives my dedication on the governing board.
My primary goal is to lead the school in fulfilling its vision and ensuring responsible allocation of resources to support our educational services. Every decision I make in this role is driven by the best interests of our students and the wider Ealing community
Emma Perkis
It has been an honour and privilege to work at John Chilton School for the past 18 years. I have had varying job roles throughout my time at John Chilton, which has given me a wealth of knowledge and experience. I have seen how dedicated and passionate our staff are in their commitment to the pupils becoming confident, motivated and independent adults when they leave school. I am currently supporting Phase 5 with their Preparation for Adulthood. I run the School Council, organize social events for our pupils and their families and run the After School Club. I look forward to making a real contribution to the strategic management of the school and working alongside other members of the Governing Board to ensure that the work we do can fulfil our duties to all the pupils.

Assessment and Target Setting
The principle of assessment is to check and identify what a child understands and what they need to learn next. It ensures that teachers can plan appropriately to enable our pupils to achieve more. Assessment is continuous throughout lessons and interventions.
To give information to parents and carers about their child’s progress:
How we Assess Progress at John Chilton School
It is recognised that progress will be individual and the expectation of how much progress each pupil will make will be considered against the individual’s: cognitive ability, syndrome, physical and sensory difficulty. Progress for one pupil may be evidenced by Achieved in a higher Stage in the school system; for another it may be recorded as being Participated in more concepts at a lower Stage. Both are regarded as equal in excellence.

What the Government says
The Government has announced that schools need to create their own assessment systems involving the following principles:
Give reliable information to parents about how their child, and their child’s school, is performing.
Help drive improvement for pupils and teachers.
Make sure the school is keeping up with external best practice and innovation

Blended Learning Offer
At John Chilton School, we have developed a range of learning approaches tailored to the diverse needs of our community. Our in-school provision includes a full curriculum complemented by therapies and social support. We also extend our learning offer to pupils who are unable to attend school due to operations or other health-related circumstances.
Our remote learning program uses a blended approach, combining online and practical activities to ensure inclusivity. This approach allows pupils to stay connected with their peers, close gaps in their learning, and feel part of the class. The content is carefully designed to match each pupils age and stage of development.
Staff collaborate closely with parents and external professionals to deliver high-quality remote learning opportunities that meet the diverse needs of all pupils.

Ofsted February 2024
With these changes in mind, leaders and staff completely overhauled the school’s curriculum. This work has been highly effective, with three curriculum pathways targeted carefully to meet different SEND needs. Across the range of subjects in each pathway, the precise knowledge that the school wants pupils to learn has been identified. Leaders and staff have a sharp focus on ensuring that the curriculum has a consistently strong impact on pupils’ learning and development. It is designed to give pupils the knowledge, skills and confidence that they need to prepare them to lead meaningful adult lives. The school’s high ambitions are met.
Curriculum Intent
At John Chilton School pupils are at the centre of the curriculum, and therefore its design and content aim to maximise the individual’s learning potential. We ensure that pupils’ personal priority needs are the starting point of their education, which we meet through personalised plans, interventions and adaptations
The curriculum is all the planned activities that we organise in order to promote learning, personal growth and development. It includes the formal requirements of the National Curriculum and, importantly, the range of additional priorities, specialist curriculum activities and therapy programmes that the school develops in order to engage, enable, empower and equip the pupils for life. It also incorporates the ethos and environment which promote the vision of the school of developing confident, independent and motivated learners.
The school has developed three pathways of learning that meet the different cohort needs of the pupils. Pupils can move between different pathways as their needs change over time. The pathways are differentiated by planning, approach and staffing support to be relevant to the cohorts of pupils.
Ambition for Pathways
The curriculum is designed, structured and sequenced to develop the knowledge and skills that the pupils are expected to gain at each phase.
Firstly, there is an ambitious intent of giving the pupils the experiences and opportunities that will develop knowledge and abilities to be an active participant in adult life. This is structured through the phases against the themes in Preparation for Adulthood and include the cultural capital they need to succeed in life.

Long term Curriculum Plans and Expected Outcomes
Subject content is planned with clear end points for each phase, while building on prior learning and taking account of the need to reinforce and recapitulate concepts to enable long term memory changes.
All pupils have access to a broad and balanced curriculum and depending on age or pathway, access this through a holistic, thematic approach or discrete subject lessons. The knowledge, skills and concepts are designated for each phase building on previous learning as the pupils move through the school. The expected outcomes for each pathway and end of phase are specified to encourage aspirational subject based learning.​
